messages:
jess: Heads-up: I want to run an overnight soak that tries to repro the intermittent ECC/Xid we've been seeing, but with an added network perturbation step (toggle fabric lanes + RDMA stress). Idea is to reproduce the failure class that only shows up when both GPU load and network reconfiguration happen.

martin: :thumbsup: when are you thinking? we should do it during the low-traffic window to avoid customer impact. also need to reserve the rack.

jess: target tonight 00:30 PST — 6h run. will pick 4 spare nodes from g2-rack-c (nodes g2-c-12,g2-c-15,g2-c-18,g2-c-21). plan:
- cordon + drain
- run burnin script with memtest+kvcache churn
- run ib_write_bw on the NIC pair to saturate interconnect every 20m for 5m
- after each saturation, run a short 1k-step token-gen load to exercise KV cache
- capture nvidia-smi -q, dmesg, kern logs, and ib stats

sam: how will we detect Xid vs ECC? i can add a live filter to the burnin logger, dump any "Xid" or "EDAC" lines to S3.

jess: yes please. pattern to watch: "NVRM: Xid (PCI:...): 79" and kernel EDAC ECC messages like "edac mc0: CE". if we get any of those, abort and snapshot all telemetry.

ops-bot: @jess created burnin job: job_id=burnin-2124567890-overnight, nodes=[g2-c-12,g2-c-15,g2-c-18,g2-c-21], window=2026-03-19T00:30-06:30Z

martin: reminder: update capacity planner — those 4 nodes are part of Dedicated pool. I can move traffic off the pool but need confirmation from platform team to avoid hitting reserved commitments.

jess: confirmed with platform. Sam will re-route traffic; I also lowered autoscaler thresholds for the night. Impact: ~6% capacity reduction in us-west.

sam: re-route done. also adding a quick healthcheck that waits 5m post-drain before starting so we don't race node teardown.

jess: snippet i'll run on each node:
```
# run on node as root
./burnin --duration 6h --gpu-all --memtest --kv-churn=heavy --log=s3://redwood-burnin/2124567890/$NODE.log
# schedule RDMA stress
for i in $(seq 1 18); do sleep 1200; ib_write_bw -F -D 300 $PEER_ADDR &
done
```

sam: added auto-abort rule: if EDAC CE count > 3 within 10m OR any Xid 79/31 show up, the run will stop and node will stay quarantined. We'll create a support ticket automatically.

jess: good. also adding a kernel parameter toggle to re-enable PCIe ASPM off during the run to see if power state transitions are correlated. i'll push that as a sysctl before starting.

martin: can you log the thermal probe timeline? last time we saw a correlation with a 3-4°C spike when RDMA bursts started.

jess: will capture ipmi and thermprobe every 30s. if we repro, steps to return to service: 1) full memtest 2) run mini-repro loop for 12h 3) if passes, bake back into pool with canary traffic for 24h. if fails, mark for RMA.

sam: tagging @oncall for overnight monitoring. oncall: can you watch the Slack channel and PagerDuty alerts for this job? we'll push quick diagnostics if you get anything.

oncall: I'm on. will watch alerts and check the burnin logs when triggers happen. add me to the S3 ACLs.

jess: done. I'll kick this off in 10. attaching quick commands to re-run repro locally if you want to iterate:
```
# repro single GPU
./burnin --duration 1h --gpu 0 --memtest --kv-churn=med
# watch logs
tail -f /var/log/syslog | egrep "Xid|EDAC|NVRM"
```

ops-bot: burnin-2124567890-overnight started for nodes [g2-c-12,g2-c-15,g2-c-18,g2-c-21] at 2026-03-19T00:31:05Z

martin: thanks. if we don't see repro, next step is longer thermal cycling + different kernel driver version (we suspect timing race in driver 525.x). we'll sync tomorrow AM with SRE/driver team.

sam: lgtm. i'll post results summary in #eng-infra in the morning with links to logs and a quick failure taxonomy if any flaky cards show up.

jess: perfect. :thumbsup:
